amendments.body: Add `crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1` to version control. It is currently untracked (`git status` shows `?? crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs`), so none of the new alkalinity/pH/budget regression coverage is actually part of the patch yet.
amendments.rationale: This change relies on new scientific-regression tests for stoichiometry, pH decline, soft-vs-hard water behavior, and budget visibility. If the file stays untracked, the implementation lands without the intended protection.

amendments.body: Fix the remaining hard-coded `mg` labels in the new alkalinity assertion paths at `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:473` and `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:495-503`. `Element::Alkalinity` now carries meq values, but these failure messages still print them as `mg`, which makes the debug output scientifically wrong when an alkalinity check fails.
amendments.rationale: The whole point of the added alkalinity tracking is explainable diagnostics. Misreporting the unit in assertion output will send future debugging and tuning in the wrong direction.

payload.summary: Reviewed the alkalinity-budget/tracing changes and ran the dedicated `nitrification_alkalinity` test target successfully. The core runtime changes look consistent, but I found two follow-ups: the new regression test file is still untracked, and the new alkalinity helper diagnostics still label meq values as mg.
